output.brief:
The stop increase comes from an interaction between two changes. The new firmware (6.4) now treats faint short-range reflections as obstacles, and the glossy stretch film on outbound pallets produces those reflections at oblique angles. Neither change causes the problem alone.

Evidence: upgraded pallet robots in Zones A/B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 robot-hours. Robots still on 6.3 in the same zones stayed flat at about 3.2. Tote robots on 6.4 in Zone C, which has no wrapped pallets, were also flat. The bench test with no people present gave 17 of 20 stops for 6.4 with gloss film. It gave 0 or 1 of 20 for every other combination. About 93% of the added stops have no person's badge within 3 m, so the temps are not the driver.

What to do: switch outbound pallets back to the previous matte film, keep firmware as is, and track stops by zone and firmware group. Don't adopt the three-strike policy or the 20% shorter protective fields. Don't rely on Halvane's December release until it is tested against the gloss film. Rolling back to 6.3 is a fallback only. Security support for 6.3 ends 31 October.

Confidence is high on the mechanism. It is lower on how much the stops contribute to the missed cut-offs, which also track the 18% volume increase.
